title: Compact objects in the derived category of a ring are perfect
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $D(A)$ denote the unbounded derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with small coproducts represented by termwise direct sums of complexes. Let $E\in D(A)$ be compact [def-pc-compact-object], meaning that for every small family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ the canonical map $\bigoplus_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(E,M_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(E,\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i)$ is bijective. Then $E$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]: there is a bounded cochain complex $F^\bullet$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules and an isomorphism $E\cong F^\bullet$ in $D(A)$. Equivalently its terms can be taken to be direct summands of finite free $A$-modules: for every degree $r$ there are $n_r\geq0$ and $A$-linear maps $F^r\xrightarrow{i_r}A^{n_r}\xrightarrow{p_r}F^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07LT, proposition-perfect-is-compact, implication (2) to (1), with definition-perfect for the bounded finite-projective model.

proof.text: Choose a complex $K^\bullet$ representing $E$. For $n\geq0$ form $T_n$ with zero terms below $n$, term $K^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ in degree $n$, and terms $K^r$ for $r>n$, with the induced differentials. The canonical quotient maps give a chain map $K^\bullet\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}T_n$: in degree $r$ only $0\leq n\leq r$ can contribute. By [lem-pc-derived-module-direct-sums] the termwise sum $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}T_n$ with the images of its coprojections is the coproduct in $D(A)$, so compactness [def-pc-compact-object] expresses its derived image as a finite sum of maps through individual summands. Projecting to an index $n$ outside that finite set gives the zero morphism $E\to Q(T_n)$. For every $r\geq n$ its cohomology map is the identity on $H^r(K)$, by the displayed quotient construction and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence $H^r(E)=0$ for every $r\geq n$. In particular choose an upper cohomological bound $b=n-1$.

source.place: Tag 07LT, proposition-perfect-is-compact, converse, first paragraph (canonical lower truncations).

proof.text: Replace $K$ by the complex $C$ equal to $K$ below $b$, to $\ker(d_K^b)$ in degree $b$, and to zero above $b$. Its inclusion into $K$ is a quasi-isomorphism: it preserves cohomology through degree $b$ and both cohomologies vanish above $b$. Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] to $C$, with $\mathcal P$ the class of all free $A$-modules, including zero. Every module is a quotient of the free module on its underlying set, by sending the generator labelled $x$ to $x$, so the covering hypothesis holds. We obtain a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ with free terms and $P^r=0$ for $r>b$. Thus $Q(P)\cong E$.

source.place: Tag 07LT, converse, bounded-above free replacement; derived.tex Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution (1), after explicit good upper truncation.

proof.text: Let $L_m=\sigma_{\geq-m}P$ for $m\geq0$, the complex equal to $P$ in degrees $r\geq-m$ and zero below. The inclusions $t_m:L_m\to L_{m+1}$ have degreewise union $P$. Put $B=\bigoplus_mL_m$, and let $s$ carry the $m$th summand to the $(m+1)$st by $t_m$. The maps $1-s:B\to B$ and $B\to P$ (sum of the inclusions) form a short exact sequence of complexes. Indeed the first nonzero coordinate proves injectivity of $1-s$; modulo its image an element of finite support is moved to a single sufficiently late coordinate, where it is zero exactly when its image in $P$ is zero. Every element of $P$ lies in a sufficiently late $L_m$, giving surjectivity. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] this gives the telescope distinguished triangle $Q(B)\xrightarrow{1-s}Q(B)\to Q(P)\to Q(B)[1]$. Since termwise sums compute the coproducts of $D(A)$ [lem-pc-derived-module-direct-sums], $Q(B)=\bigoplus_mQ(L_m)$ with $Q(1-s)$ as $1-\mathrm{shift}$, and [lem-pc-compact-hom-hocolim] applies to the compact $E$. The isomorphism $E\to Q(P)$ factors through some $Q(L_m)$. Compose the inclusion with $Q(P)\cong E$ to obtain maps $\varphi:E\to Q(L_m)$ and $\psi:Q(L_m)\to E$ with $\psi\varphi=1_E$. This $L_m$ is bounded and free, but its ranks need not yet be finite.

source.place: Tag 07LT, converse, stupid truncations and factorization of the identity; Tag 07LR, lemma-commutes-with-countable-sums, telescope calculation; derived.tex Tag 094A.

proof.text:
Fix bounds $[a,b]$ for this bounded free complex $L$. We induct on $c=a,a+1,\ldots,b+1$, maintaining maps $E\xrightarrow{\varphi}Q(L)\xrightarrow{\psi}E$ with composite $1_E$, the same bounds, free terms, and finite free terms in degrees $r<c$. At $c=a$ the last condition is vacuous. For the induction step $c\leq b$, choose a basis $L^c= igoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A$. The images of the finitely many basis vectors of $L^{c-1}$ have support in a finite subset $S_0\subset\Lambda$ (if $c=a$, the source is zero). Consequently projection in degree $c$ defines a chain map $\pi_0:L	o igoplus_{\lambda
otin S_0}A[-c]$: its only chain-map condition is $\pi_0d^{c-1}=0$. The termwise sum $ igoplus_{\lambda
otin S_0}A[-c]$ is the coproduct of the $A[-c]$ in $D(A)$ [lem-pc-derived-module-direct-sums], so compactness [def-pc-compact-object] says $Q(\pi_0)\varphi$ factors through a finite subcoproduct indexed by $S_1\subset\Lambda\setminus S_0$. Enlarge $S_0$ to $S=S_0\cup S_1$. The resulting projection $\pi:L	o igoplus_{\lambda
otin S}A[-c]$ satisfies $Q(\pi)\varphi=0$, because it kills every summand in the finite factorization.

source.place: Tag 07LT, converse, finite-basis induction paragraph, through the enlargement of the finite subset.

proof.text: Let $L'=\ker\pi$ degreewise. It agrees with $L$ except that $(L')^c=A^S$, and its inherited differentials make it a subcomplex since $\pi$ is a chain map. Projection $\pi$ is surjective in every degree, so [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] gives the distinguished triangle $Q(L')\xrightarrow{j}Q(L)\xrightarrow{Q(\pi)}\bigoplus_{\lambda\notin S}A[-c]\to Q(L')[1]$. Apply clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] with $W=E$ to the equality $Q(\pi)\varphi=0$. It supplies $\varphi':E\to Q(L')$ with $j\varphi'=\varphi$. Set $\psi'=\psi j$; then $\psi'\varphi'=\psi\varphi=1_E$. The new complex has unchanged bounds, all terms remain free, and now every term in degree $r<c+1$ is finite free. This proves the induction step. After $b-a+1$ steps, the identity of $E$ factors through a bounded finite free complex $F$.

source.place: Tag 07LT, converse, kernel triangle and lifting in the finite-basis induction.

proof.text: Write the resulting maps as $i:E\to Q(F)$ and $p:Q(F)\to E$ with $pi=1_E$. Complete $i$ to a distinguished triangle $E\xrightarrow{i}Q(F)\to C\xrightarrow{\delta}E[1]$, using the triangulated structure in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Applying the zero-composite clause of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to its rotated triangle gives $i[1]\delta=0$ (the rotation sign is irrelevant to zero). Multiplying by $p[1]$ gives $\delta=0$. Hence [lem-pc-derived-zero-third-split] gives $Q(F)\cong E\oplus C$. The finite free terms of $F$ are finitely generated projective: generators are the standard basis, and any map from a finite free module lifts along a surjection by lifting its basis images, as in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Thus $Q(F)$ is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Applying [lem-sf-perfect-ring-summand] proves that $E$ is perfect, which by the same definition supplies the required bounded finite projective model.

source.place: Tag 07LT, final converse paragraph; Tag 066S, lemma-summands-perfect. The existing retraction is converted to a biproduct by the zero-third-map splitting lemma instead of splitting a new idempotent.

proof.text: For the final equivalent formulation, let $M$ be any finitely generated projective term in the bounded model. Choose a finite set of generators, giving a surjection $q:A^n\to M$. The lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], applied to $1_M$, gives $i:M\to A^n$ with $qi=1_M$; take $p=q$. Conversely, for a specified pair $i:M\to A^n$, $p:A^n\to M$ with $pi=1$, the elements $p(e_j)$ generate $M$, and a map $f:M\to N$ lifts along a surjection $N'\to N$ by first lifting the basis images of $fp:A^n\to N$ and then composing the lift with $i$. Thus $M$ is finitely generated projective. Applying this separately to every term proves the stated equivalence, including rank zero outside the bounded interval.
